claims.statement: At the pinned snapshot, stopped codespaces are automatically deleted after a defined inactive interval. Retention is fixed when each codespace is created and does not change for that instance; the documented default is 30 days. This is a lifecycle-risk reference, not a verified current configuration, backup receipt or instruction to delete.

The machine-change procedure uses the editor command palette, selects a target when outside a codespace and otherwise applies to the current codespace, then selects a machine type. A different storage capacity adds a continuation prompt that the source says to read before accepting. No prompt was accepted or machine changed; screenshot captions were read but image assets were not visually reviewed.

The fragment points to a separate storage-troubleshooting section for determining whether the default dev container image was used. A link alone supplies neither the determination procedure nor evidence of the actual image.

The editor navigation instruction selects Remote Explorer and includes a further indented remote-explorer reusable fragment. The include and screenshot asset remain separate dependencies; this source read does not prove rendered navigation, connection or authorization.

Codespace logs describe codespace, container, session and editor-environment details useful in diagnosing connection and unexpected-behavior examples. Example symptoms are not a diagnosis or verified fix; no real logs or private session details were collected.

Continuing beyond included monthly compute and storage is described as requiring payment details and a spending limit, with a linked billing explanation. This optional paid-use path is not authority to change financial settings, approve costs or guarantee continued availability.

Available machine choices can be constrained by organization policy or repository minimum specifications among other factors. The two linked policy/specification procedures remain separate evidence; no actual allowed set or effective policy has been verified.

The pinned fragment describes typical machine choices from 2 to 32 cores while qualifying that the full range may be unavailable; types have different resources and billing tiers. Default creation selects the lowest valid resources, not necessarily the smallest globally offered machine. Snapshot capabilities do not verify current pricing, eligibility or authorize costs.
